title: How conditions are inherited
summary: We each have two copies of most genes, one from each parent. How a condition passes from parents to children depends on its inheritance pattern.
body: Autosomal recessive: a child needs a changed copy from both parents to be affected; people with one changed copy are healthy carriers. Autosomal dominant: one changed copy is enough to cause the condition. X-linked: the gene is on the X chromosome, so boys and girls are affected differently. The chances are the same for every pregnancy; earlier children do not change them. Dominant and X-linked patterns are more complex in families, so a genetic counsellor should go through them with you.
